source.description: Fixed XEd25519 signature vectors, X25519 agreement vectors and Curve25519 public-key range vectors found in libsignal v0.99.1 (the libsignal-client bundled with signal-cli v0.14.7). libsignal's XEd25519 deviates from the signal.org XEdDSA spec in how the Edwards sign bit is carried (see spec/crypto/xeddsa.md); every signature here verifies only under libsignal's rule. No upstream test fixes the 64-byte random input Z, so no vector here pins signing output; all signature vectors are verify-only. The signal.org XEdDSA document (Revision 1, 2016-10-20) contains no test vectors. Every positive signature vector below was also checked by the spec agent with OpenSSL Ed25519 verification after the Montgomery-to-Edwards conversion described in xeddsa.md; X25519 agreement and public-key derivations were checked with OpenSSL X25519.
source.conventions: All byte strings are lowercase hex. Curve25519 private keys are 32 bytes as given upstream (libsignal clamps them on import). public_key_with_prefix = 0x05 || 32-byte Montgomery u (libsignal's serialized form); public_key_without_prefix = the 32-byte u. Signatures are 64 bytes R || S where the top bit of the final byte carries the Edwards sign bit of the signer's public key.

vectors.upstream_test: rust/core/src/curve/curve25519.rs tests::test_signature; java Curve25519Test.testSignature (same data)
vectors.message_note: The message is the 33-byte serialized (0x05-prefixed) public key of Alice's ephemeral key, i.e. the same shape as a signed-prekey signature input.
vectors.random_input_note: Not fixed upstream (signature was produced elsewhere with unknown Z).
